identity.covers: the declaring module, every package module its code calls — the frozen geometry and board model it imports and Experiment 002's reachable-set enumeration it reuses — and, since the 63e432f round, the agent wrapper that produces the choices: the module that defines the agent factory, which selects the class, and the class whose _choose hands the objective every state parameter it reads (the board, the current and preview pieces, the level, the lines, the start level, the first-delay countdown, the ruleset and the mode) and executes the placement it returns. The digest of each covered module is the source the interpreter loaded, fixed by the loader that read it and revised by exactly one event — a load — so a module the process reloads is recorded as the code that computes the choices; the writer reads the loader's current digests when the run or live session is constructed, not a later read of module.__file__, which is only a path (the 9799d59e round's bug) and not an import-time snapshot either (the 38e6904c round's); a closure a *partial* reload left inconsistent — one module reloaded while the modules that imported its objects keep them, the callers that hold the factory by value included — is refused rather than recorded, because no single digest describes both The set is discovered from the code rather than hand-listed — the objective's own namespace and the module that defines the factory, from which the class it returns is reached — so a module that stops producing choices drops out of the identity by itself, and neither a helper's change nor a wrapper's can move the objective's values unrecorded. The wrapper imports the objective rather than the other way round, which is why the walk that stopped at the objective's own imports could not reach it
identity.gating: required at version 6, the version the current writer emits, under the shape that covers the wrapper; a version-5 record is compared against the older shape its own writer recorded — the modules the objective's own imports reach — because that is the identity it carries and the retained version-5 records must keep verifying. Optional at version 4 and 2, whose writers recorded no identity, and compared when present
identity.value: one sha256 per package module the objective's choices are computed from, keyed by module name
identity.why: the weights are constants, so a formula change that leaves them alone changes every value the objective computes while the recorded weights still compare equal, and the replayed choices catch it only when the change happens to move one of them. The reviewer's counterexample — the clear term charging a premature clear at twice the declared rate — keeps every weight and is reported by this identity alone; and the wrapper could hand the objective a different state parameter or bypass the objective altogether while the recorded seeds kept exactly their actions, which the identity misses as long as it stops at the objective's own imports — the finding this round repairs, executed as prechange_probe.py objective_wrapper_identity; and the identity is read from each module's path at the moment the writer imports it, so a file edited between a module's own import and the writer's import is recorded though the loaded code chose the inputs — the finding the 9799d59e round repairs, executed as prechange_probe.py loaded_identity
